chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, and Abu al-Abbas Muhammad ibn Ja'far al-Razzaz from Ayoub ibn Nuh, and Humayd ibn Ziyad from Ibn Sama'ah, all from Safwan, from Ibn Muskan, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

When a man divorces his wife before consummating the marriage with her, she is irrevocably divorced from him, and she may marry if she wishes from that very moment; and if he had stipulated a dower for her, then she is entitled to half of the dower; and if he had not stipulated a dower for her, then he should provide her with gifts (mut'ah).

key_terms.فَلَهَا نِصْفُ الْمَهْرِ: she is entitled to half the dower
key_terms.فَلْيُمَتِّعْهَا: he should provide her with gifts/provision (mut'ah)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on dower and remarriage for a woman divorced before consummation in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the fiqh of khula' or talaq before consummation, establishing that the marital bond is severed immediately, allowing for instant remarriage without a waiting period (iddah). It distinguishes between the financial rights of the wife: she is entitled to half the stipulated mahr if one was agreed upon, or a discretionary gift (mut'ah) if no mahr was specified, reflecting the Prophetic practice of fairness in partial marital dissolution. This ruling is foundational in Shia jurisprudence for determining the status of women in pre-consummation divorces.
